scope: Private TradingView compile, saved-script creation, chart instantiation, 60-source binding readback and budget observation on an isolated shadow layout. Not publication, not a managed layout change, not Suite/Breakout parity, and not rollback evidence.

bindingReadback.persistenceNote: A force-rebind run reports 60/60 inside its own session even when nothing persists: tv_verify_consumer_bindings.ts clicks the settings submit button but never calls saveChangedChartLayout, and submit only mutates the in-memory instance. The first read-only reload during this session returned 60/60 'Close' for exactly that reason. The recorded result comes from a rebind and layout save performed in one session, re-read in a fresh session.

budgets.drawingObjectNote: Both scripts use plot/plotshape/fill only, so no drawing-object budget is consumed.

nonInterference.note: The R2.4 Hold Manager layout twh98JLB was not opened. No Suite instance exists on this layout, so the 'Context results alter a Suite decision or alert' condition is structurally excluded rather than merely unobserved.

openGates: Compare structure and zone output with Suite and Breakout evidence and explain discrepancies; no recorded Suite/Breakout structure-zone evidence set exists in the repository yet.
Run the rollback drill (remove both scripts from the shadow layout and save) — not executed here, so the shadow remains established.
Decide whether the private saved script satisfies the 'privately publish' wording of the R4-BUS gate or whether a TradingView publish step is additionally required.

rollbackDrill.procedure: Remove SMC Context Overlay and SMC Context Bus from the shadow layout, save the layout.
rollbackDrill.managedSurfacesNote: No managed script (Suite, Dashboard, Strategy, Alerts, Hold Manager) was present on the layout before or after the drill, so 'verify those existing surfaces remain unchanged' holds structurally: the rollback had no managed surface to touch.
rollbackDrill.note: Both the removal and the restoration were confirmed in a FRESH session, not only inside the mutating run — the same standard applied to the original binding evidence.

publishWording.question: Does the private saved script satisfy the R4-BUS 'privately publish' gate?
evidence: .github/workflows/tv-save-consumer-source.yml: 'Unlike the library publishers, consumers are not "published"; they are the operator\'s saved chart scripts.'
CLAUDE.md: publishing is repo -> TradingView for Pine LIBRARIES only.
scripts/tv_publish_micro_library.ts lists SMC Long-Dip Suite (the Engine BUS v2 producer) as a library CONSUMER with role 'producer'; the Suite itself is never published.
publishWording.conclusion: SMC Context Bus is handled exactly like the Engine BUS v2 producer: a private saved chart script. No TradingView publish step is required for this gate.

suiteBreakoutComparison.finding: All 60 CTX channels are plotted with display = display.none on the producer, and the 60 consumer inputs carry display.none as well. TradingView renders display.none nowhere, not even in the Data Window, so the channel VALUES cannot be read from the UI for a numeric parity comparison.
suiteBreakoutComparison.visibleSurface: Only the overlay's own rendering is visible (8 plots, 10 plotshapes, 7 fills), which supports a qualitative visual check, not the value parity the gate asks for.
suiteBreakoutComparison.requiredNext: A fixture-only readback, following the R2.4 precedent: the readback lives in a generated TEST ONLY fixture derived from the canonical source, never in the production surface, and is never published. Method decided 2026-08-01, see docs/SMC_R4_CONTEXT_READBACK_DECISION.md.
suiteBreakoutComparison.requiredNextAmendmentReason: The original wording said a second competing observability mechanism was 'explicitly ruled out by the R2.4 outcome', and that claim is not supported by the R2.4 record. No R2.4 artifact or document states such a rule; the record documents a procedure (exact-hash approval, private TEST ONLY script, isolated layout, not published, canonical state restored), not a prohibition. The precedent it cites is in fact an instance of BUILDING a readback: SMC_Hold_Manager.pine contains no table.new at all while the R2.4 fixture contains eight. What the precedent rules out is a readback in the PRODUCTION surface, not a readback as such. The measurement in 'finding' above is unchanged: it is a dated observation and stays as captured.
